drafted_from: tool:sum-a-characters-time-per-video's row in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/ and the tests in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Sum the parrot's time in each episode against how the videos did, with the first 20 seconds and the last 10 counted on their own." It runs tool:sum-a-characters-time-per-video and writes character-per-video.tsv.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one settings row of yours (record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) or the settings you pass, and works on files in the show's folder.
instructions: 1. Make the show's folder and the YouTube library folder the run may change, and have the catalog.tsv and voice/<id>.turns.json for the videos. Put the keys the row needs (opening_seconds, closing_seconds, stripped_ids, compare_from_month, compare_to_month, lowest_from_year) in your settings row or pass them as settings.

2. Say the sentence in start_here to your AI. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:sum-a-characters-time-per-video and the input in the worked example; the door asks for the granted folder.
3. Read the last line it prints, {"result": ...}, or {"error": ...} saying what to fix (a missing settings key is named).
4. Read the tables printed by year and the table character-per-video.tsv; the comparison of the stripped episodes needs at least one stripped id with turns.

worked_examples.title: One scored episode of two
worked_examples.ask: How much does the parrot talk per episode?
worked_examples.given: From the sample run in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json and PerVideoTest in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/test_measures.py: the catalog holds vid-a (1000 views, x_baseline 1.5) and vid-c (stripped); only vid-a has a turns file, with three turns [10,12], [15,17] and [40,42] in 100.0 s.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"table": "{grant:change-a-folder}/show/character-per-video.tsv", "scored": 1, "episodes": 1, "stripped_median": null, "full_median": 1.5}}; the vid-a row is turns 3, character_s 6.0, share 0.06, open_s 4.0, outro_s 0, body_exchanges 1, ex_per_10min 8.57, stripped False; with no year holding six videos the thirds print low 0 | mid 0 | high 0.
